items.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Paul Currian wrote things about your recordings; INTERVIEWEE responds to the quote about Coltrane but does not mention Currian or their relationship.

ctx.x: That’s a bit of an oxymoron, yeah. Before we leave Coltrane, there was a fella named Paul Currian who wrote some things about your recordings. And he just had this statement about Coltrane and I wanted to read it and see if you have a reaction to it: “Coltrane was aiming for some kind of transcendence, a destination which many of his early fans were simply not interested in following him to, considering the reception given to his later recordings and performances.” Did you follow John Coltrane’s music all the way…

Well my interest was actually how he created this intense feeling of playing. I mean he was an artist. I mean he was almost like, you know he would be able to really just delve on just one of two things you know, not intricate but I mean to get that feeling of, I mean I have some cuts you know that he goes really — it’s not — analytically it’s not really a big thing but I mean the creation that he really has applied. I mean he was — that was the thing actually I suppose, and everybody does feel that way too when…
